name: Ancient Mesopotamia
region: Tigris-Euphrates River System (Modern Iraq, Kuwait, Syria, Turkey)
description: Widely known as the 'Cradle of Civilization', where the earliest complex urban settlements, monumental architecture, and codified laws first emerged.

name: Ancient Egypt
description: One of the longest-lasting civilizations in human history, flourishing along the fertile banks of the Nile, unified under pharaohs and famous for monumental architecture, religion, and military prowess.

name: Indus Valley Civilization (Harappan Civilization)
region: Indus River Basin (Modern Pakistan and Northwestern India)
description: A Bronze Age civilization in South Asia renowned for its peaceful urbanism, advanced sanitation, maritime dockyards (Lothal), and undeciphered script.

name: Classical Greece
description: A transformative era of intellectual and political flourishing that laid the foundational pillars of Western philosophy, political theory, scientific inquiry, and the arts.

name: Roman Empire
period: 27 BC – 476 AD (Western Empire); until 1453 AD (Eastern Byzantine Empire)
region: Mediterranean Basin, Southern/Western Europe, North Africa, Levant
description: The post-Republican period of ancient Rome with an autocratic government and vast territorial holdings around the Mediterranean Sea ('Mare Nostrum').

name: The Renaissance
origin: Florence, Italy (expanding across Western and Northern Europe)
description: A fervent period of European cultural, artistic, political, and economic rebirth following the Middle Ages, marked by the rediscovery of classical philosophy, literature, and art.

name: The Industrial Revolution
origin: Great Britain (spreading to Western Europe and North America)
description: The transition from agrarian, handcrafted economies to ones dominated by mechanized industry, machine manufacturing, urban factory systems, and unprecedented economic expansion.
